blocks.content:
Igneous — cooling magma
Sedimentary — compressed sediments
Metamorphic — heat & pressure

items: Questions frequently test the primary agent of formation: Igneous (magma cooling) vs. Metamorphic (heat & pressure).
Remember that Sedimentary rock formation specifically requires the compression of accumulated sediments.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Igneous rocks are formed through the cooling and solidification of molten magma.
Sedimentary rocks result from the accumulation, compaction, and compression of mineral sediments.
Metamorphic rocks are created when existing rock types undergo transformation due to extreme heat and high pressure.
